records.title: Five reported completed developments
labels: Reported completed in draft FY2025–26 CAPER
Calculated from five draft CAPER project rows
summary: Phoenix’s draft FY2025–26 CAPER reports completion of 25th @ Bell (53 apartments), Pueblo Apartments (161), Garfield II (60), Residences at Falcon Park (192) and Harmony at the Park III (90).
The five developments total 556 apartments and 49 HOME-designated units as reported in the draft FY2025–26 CAPER.
context: PHX-WEB-001 · Five distinct developments, not all Phoenix housing production Reporting period: 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30
Scope Five reported completed projects only Time period FY2025–26
PHX-WEB-002 · Calculated report subtotal
limitations: A draft report is not a verified certificate of occupancy, fully occupied property or HUD acceptance. The public copy remained draft when checked.

records.title: Girasol: redevelopment and dated progress
labels: Planned gross redevelopment units; not completed production
Construction progress and forecasts as of October 26, 2026
summary: Girasol, the final Edison-Eastlake phase on the former 145-unit Sidney P. Osborn site, is planned for 364 apartments: 289 affordable and 75 market-rate.

The October 26, 2026 update reported Girasol Phase I construction 82% complete and Phase II 79% complete. It forecast their move-ins in early 2027, Phase III construction in Q1 2027 and Phase III move-ins in 2028.
context: Scope Three Girasol subphases on the former Sidney P. Osborn site Time period Project card revised October 26, 2026
PHX-WEB-020 · Official GO Bond project scope

limitations: Keep in mind. 364 counts all planned newly constructed apartments, including redevelopment of existing housing capacity. It is not 364 net additions or 364 new affordable units. Exact legal replacement obligations are a separate measure.
Construction percentages are not occupied-unit counts. Planned future starts and move-ins must not be marked completed.

records.title: Capital Fund: obligation, draw and expenditure definitions
labels: HUD program definitions · Not Phoenix transaction evidence
summary: PHA obligation: a binding agreement for work or financing that will result in outlays.
Grant draw: Capital Funds vouchered through HUD’s Line of Credit Control System (LOCCS).
HUD grant-reporting expenditure: the PHA pays a contractor or vendor bill using funds disbursed from LOCCS.
context: Scope HUD Capital Fund guidance for public housing agencies (PHAs); national definitions, not a Phoenix ledger. Period and source date HUD training materials dated September 25, 2023.
Financial stage: Definitions separating a PHA commitment, a grant disbursement and expenditure.
PHX-CFP-WEB-006
limitations: What this does not show A PHA obligation is different from HUD’s federal award obligation. This HUD grant-reporting definition of expenditure is distinct from the SEFA accounting measure. These definitions do not establish Phoenix’s amounts, dates or completion of grant-processing requirements.
